Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the conversation yesterday. Attached are HealthGrid's redlines to the DPA and our proposed SCCs. Before we exchange formal counter-redlines, a few clarifications we'd like Redwood to confirm: 

- Processor/subprocessor approvals: HealthGrid requires written approval for any new subprocessor onboarding for the services that process health data. The draft DPA currently states Redwood will provide "notice" only. Can Redwood confirm whether written approval is possible, or alternatively provide an operational SLA for notice + objection + approval window?

- Transfer Impact Addendum: please confirm the concrete mitigations Redwood can commit to for EU-to-US transfers. Specifically: KMS key scoping (can keys be scoped per-customer?), whether keys can be resident in an EU-only KMS for the HealthGrid account, and whether Redwood would sign supplementary transfer paperwork if required.

- Data return / deletion: HealthGrid needs a 30-day secure export window post-termination and a certificate of secure deletion. The MSA currently references 14 days. Can Redwood accommodate 30 days?

- Subprocessor list & attestations: we'll need a timeboxed schedule for subprocessor evidence (SOC2 + encryption in transit/resident region statements) for the processors that will handle our EU data.

Attachments: HealthGrid_DPA_Redlines_20280819.docx (docx)

Can we book 30 minutes tomorrow (Aug 20) to walk through these items before legal do a tracked redline exchange? Prefer 14:00 PT. If Redwood prefers, we can move the meeting to Aug 21.

Hi Amy — thanks for sending these over and for flagging the high-priority items. Appreciate the specificity.

Quick responses to the asks above so we can be productive on a call: 

- Subprocessor approvals: Redwood's standard practice has been to provide notice and an objection right; written prior approval is an exception we can consider for customers with regulated data (we treat as an "approval-limited" addendum). Operationally we can commit to a 10-business-day review window for any new subprocessor onboarding for HealthGrid's regulated workloads, with an escalation path to our Legal/Trust team. I'll propose language that gives HealthGrid approval rights limited to regulated processing.

- KMS / transfer mitigations: we can scope KMS keys per-customer in Dedicated or Private deployments; for hosted accounts we offer a multi-tenant KMS with customer-specific key wrapping. We cannot promise EU-resident KMS for standard hosted plans without a Private deployment request, but we can propose contractual mitigations (SCCs + contractual assurances + additional audit rights) and a time-limited plan to evaluate EU-resident key options.

- Data return window: we can extend to a 30-day export window on the Order Form for HealthGrid for a regulated-data addendum. We'll confirm deletion certificate language.

- Evidence schedule: Operations can provide a subprocessor evidence snapshot (SOC2 summary, TLS, specified residency) within 7 business days of a request; for a full attestation we may need 14-21 days depending on the subprocessor.

I attached a short proposed response doc that we can iterate on the call. Can we meet Aug 21 at 14:00 PT (you indicated a preference for Aug 20 but our Legal lead is out tomorrow). Proposed dial-in below.

Amy — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. Below are our tracked answers; attached is an annotated DPA with inline comments. If anything below is inconsistent with your redlines, call it out on the call and we'll adjust.

1) Subprocessor onboarding / approvals
On Sun, 19 Aug 2028 at 09:12 Amy Ross <amy.ross@healthgrid.com> wrote:
> We need written approval for any new subprocessor onboarding for services that process health data.

Our position: Redwood accepts a controlled-approval flow for HealthGrid's regulated processing scope. Proposed clause: "Redwood will provide written notice of any new subprocessor that will process HealthGrid's regulated data. HealthGrid shall have ten (10) business days from receipt of notice to provide written objection. If HealthGrid objects, parties shall use good faith efforts to resolve. If unresolved, Redwood will not onboard the new subprocessor for HealthGrid's regulated workloads until agreement is reached or an alternative subprocessor acceptable to HealthGrid is identified."

Impact: Operationally, we will require an "approval-limited" flag on the account. This is implementable for hosted accounts but may limit ability to burst to shared pools for those workloads; we will outline expected throughput/availability tradeoffs in the Order Form appendix.

2) KMS scoping and EU-resident keys
On Sun, 19 Aug 2028 at 09:12 Amy Ross <amy.ross@healthgrid.com> wrote:
> Can keys be scoped per-customer? Can keys be resident in an EU-only KMS?

Our position: Key scoping per-customer is supported via customer-specific key wrapping in hosted plans. EU-resident KMS is achievable only via Private/Dedicated deployments. For hosted customers, we propose contract-level mitigations (SCCs + documented cryptographic controls + right to audit). If HealthGrid requires EU-resident keys, we will provide an Order Form addendum and a project estimate for migration.

3) Data return / deletion window
On Sun, 19 Aug 2028 at 09:12 Amy Ross <amy.ross@healthgrid.com> wrote:
> We need a 30 day secure export window and certificate of deletion.

Our position: Redwood will update the Order Form to provide a 30-calendar-day secure export window for accounts processing regulated data under HealthGrid's Order Form. Redwood will also provide a certificate of deletion within 10 business days of confirmed deletion.

4) Evidence & subprocessor attestation timeline
We can provide a snapshot with key attestations (SOC2 status, TLS, high-level residency) within 7 business days. Full vendor attestations may require 14-21 days depending on third-party timelines. We'll include an attachment mapping the typical scope of evidence per subprocessor.

Next steps:
- We will circulate an annotated DPA (attached) and a short Order Form addendum for "Regulated Data — HealthGrid" by EOD today.
- Call scheduled: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 at 14:00 PT (30 mins). I'll invite Ops/Trust. Please confirm Amy and your team can attend.
